answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the harbor identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 329 runs and collects one. Because the trellis index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the willow audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 329 answers need 329 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
